skill.name: storage-debug-instrumentation
skill.description: Add debugging and observability instrumentation for PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, FastAPI startup metrics, and a Next.js storage debug dashboard.
skill.summary: Add storage diagnostics, startup timing, and a Next.js debug dashboard for PostgreSQL and ChromaDB services.
skill.author: BenderFendor

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code for file paths, function names, API routes, and localhost verification examples. Two low-risk reconnaissance markers are real because the skill intentionally exposes storage and startup diagnostics. The main added risk is a high-severity semantic finding: raw debug endpoints and a dashboard are specified without authentication, redaction, or environment-gating guidance.

remediation.issue: Debug endpoints expose raw storage and startup data.
remediation.suggestion: Require authentication, role checks, and environment gating before enabling debug routes outside local development.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic responses may reveal article contents, vector metadata, IDs, timing data, and backend topology.
remediation.suggestion: Redact sensitive fields, cap sample sizes, and return only the minimum metadata needed for troubleshooting.

remediation.issue: The verification checklist includes a local external command.
remediation.suggestion: Document that commands should run only with user approval and prefer project-pinned tooling where possible.

content.value_statement: Storage drift and startup latency are hard to diagnose across databases and vector stores. This skill guides teams to add focused debug endpoints, metrics, and a dashboard.
actual_capabilities: Defines a StartupMetrics service for phase timing, notes, and app-wide reporting.
Shows where to instrument FastAPI startup and vector store initialization.
Specifies paginated PostgreSQL article inspection with filters.
Specifies ChromaDB article browsing and ID listing for drift checks.
Adds planned debug API routes for startup, ChromaDB, database, and drift reports.
Outlines a Next.js debug dashboard with timeline, tables, filters, and summary metrics.
limitations: Does not include authentication or access-control instructions for debug routes.
Does not provide ready-made code files; it describes implementation steps.
Assumes a FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, and Next.js frontend.
Requires local verification before use in shared or production environments.

use_cases.title: Trace Storage Drift
use_cases.description: Compare PostgreSQL article mappings with ChromaDB IDs to find missing or dangling records.

use_cases.title: Measure Startup Bottlenecks
use_cases.description: Record startup phases so slow database, cache, scheduler, or vector-store work is visible.

use_cases.title: Inspect Debug Dashboard Behavior
use_cases.description: Review tables, filters, pagination, and summary metrics before enabling a diagnostics page.

prompt_templates.title: Add Startup Metrics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for backend timing instrumentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add startup phase metrics to my FastAPI backend. Keep the first pass limited to timing events and notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Storage Inspection
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate backend work for database and vector-store diagnostics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add paginated PostgreSQL and ChromaDB inspection helpers. Include filters, limits, offsets, and drift comparison support.

prompt_templates.title: Build Debug Dashboard
prompt_templates.scenario: Frontend implementation for a diagnostics page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create the Next.js debug dashboard. Include startup timing, ChromaDB browsing, database browsing, and drift report tabs.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Debug Instrumentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before shared or production deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill as a baseline, then add authentication, environment gating, response redaction, tests, and safe defaults for all debug routes.

output_examples.input: Request: Add startup timing for backend boot phases.
output: A startup metrics service records phase names, durations, details, and notes.
FastAPI startup wraps database, scheduler, cache, RSS, and migration phases.
A debug endpoint returns a readable timeline for local diagnosis.

output_examples.input: Request: Find whether ChromaDB and PostgreSQL are out of sync.
output: Database helpers return article pages and article-to-vector mappings.
Vector-store helpers list document previews and stored IDs.
A drift report summarizes missing and dangling entries with bounded samples.

output_examples.input: Request: Create a dashboard for storage diagnostics.
output: The dashboard presents startup timing, ChromaDB records, PostgreSQL records, and drift data.
Filters and pagination help narrow the data without loading every record.
Summary metrics make boot time, article counts, vector counts, and drift counts visible.

best_practices: Protect debug routes with authentication and environment gates before exposing them outside local development.
Limit returned fields and redact article content when diagnostics do not need full records.
Add tests for pagination, filters, and drift counts before enabling the dashboard.
anti_patterns: Publishing debug endpoints on a public host without authentication.
Returning full database rows or vector documents to every dashboard user.
Treating startup metrics as business telemetry without retention and privacy rules.

faq.question: What systems does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets a FastAPI backend with PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, and a Next.js frontend.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready debug endpoints?
faq.answer: No. It describes diagnostics that need authentication, redaction, and environment controls before production use.

faq.question: Can it detect storage drift?
faq.answer: Yes. It specifies helpers that compare ChromaDB IDs with PostgreSQL mappings and report missing or dangling entries.

faq.question: Does it change the database schema?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that the work is additive instrumentation and debug routing only.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I verify after implementation?
faq.answer: Verify endpoint responses, dashboard loading, pagination, filters, refresh behavior, and non-zero startup phase durations.
